headline: Hormuz Accounts Still Do Not Establish One Operation
deck: A UKMTO report near Khasab and Iran’s MQ-9 claim widened the record without connecting the reports.
body: On Friday, UKMTO said it had received a report of an incident 11 nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman. Reuters later reported that UKMTO had described an outbound tanker hit by an unidentified projectile in that area. [E1][E2]

Also on Friday, Iran’s Islamic Revolution Guards Corps said it had destroyed what it described as a 58th U.S. MQ-9 over the Strait of Hormuz with a newly deployed air-defense system. That was the IRGC’s claim, not a confirmed account of an aircraft loss. [E3]

Since this paper’s 20 November coverage, the record has added the report near Khasab and the IRGC’s MQ-9 account. The report places an incident near Khasab, while the Iranian statement places its claimed drone loss over the strait; neither record names a shared operation, responsible party or connection between them. [E1][E3]

**The desk's reading.** The reports widened the Hormuz record but did not establish one operation. The strongest alternative is that the incidents formed a connected escalation; their shared waterway and date leave that possible, but the available accounts do not tie the tanker incident to the claimed drone loss.

**The next test.** By 14:00 UTC, an official account that names the reported Khasab incident and the claimed MQ-9 loss as parts of one operation would support the connection; separate official accounts identifying distinct operations would point the other way.
